metaDescription: Every lender in your statements by name, what each takes a month, how much of your income goes to EMIs, and which loan to close first.
title: EMIs, loans and subscriptions
intro: Every lender in your statements, by name: banks, NBFCs, loan apps and pay-later services. What each takes a month, what kind of loan it looks like, and which usually costs the most to keep. Your subscriptions, running and stopped, are here too.
none: No EMIs, loans or pay-later payments in your statements. Upload more months if you think something is missing.
tileLendersNote: Banks, NBFCs, apps and pay later
tileShareNote: Of about {income} a month that comes in regularly
tileShareUnknownNote: Shows once your salary repeats in your statements
tileBouncesNote: In the last 12 months of statements
band_ok: Comfortable: your EMIs take {percent} of your regular income, under 30%.
band_stretched: Stretched: your EMIs take {percent} of your regular income. Lenders usually want all EMIs under about 40 to 50%, so a new loan may be refused or cost more.
band_heavy: Heavy: your EMIs take {percent} of your regular income. One bad month can mean a bounced EMI, a fee and a mark on your credit score. Paying down the costliest loan first eases it fastest.
stackText: You are paying {count} pay-later services and loan apps at the same time. Paying one with another is how small amounts turn into a debt trap. Close the smallest first, and keep one at most.
closeIntro: If you have spare money, paying extra on the loan at the top usually saves the most. The order follows what each kind of loan usually costs; the actual rate is in your loan papers or the lender's app.
prepayNote: RBI does not allow banks and NBFCs to charge for closing or prepaying a floating-rate loan taken by an individual for a non-business purpose. For fixed-rate loans, check the foreclosure charge first.
borrowed: {amount} came in from this lender: most likely the loan itself.
lockedTitle: See every lender, and which to close first
lockedText: Subscribers see each lender by name, the kind of loan, how much of their income goes to EMIs, failed payments, and the order to close them in.
planIntro: Statements show the EMI, not the balance or the rate. Add those from your loan account or app, and Horizon works out the rest. Fixed-rate arithmetic: a floating rate moves, so this is an estimate at today's rate.
planNeed: Enter the outstanding amount and the rate to see the plan.
planNoCover: At this rate the EMI does not even cover the interest, so the loan would never end. Check the figures.
planBaseline: As it is: {months} months to go, {interest} more in interest, done around {date}.
planFaster: With the extra: {months} months to go, {interest} in interest, done around {date}.
planSaved: Saved. The figures stay with this loan.
planErr: Check the figures: a positive amount, and a rate between 0 and 60.
planSchedule: {paid} of {tenure} EMIs paid, {remaining} to go, ends around {date}.
planRemainingTotal: About {amount} still to pay at this EMI.
planOutstandingEstimated: Outstanding estimated at {amount} from the EMI, the rate and the months left; type the lender's figure if it differs.
planDueDay: Which day of the month is it due?
subsIntro: Streaming, apps and memberships that charge you on a rhythm: what they cost together, which have stopped, and what each has taken so far.
subsNone: No subscriptions found in your statements.
subsTileYearlyNote: What the running ones add up to
subsLocked: Subscribers see each subscription, running and stopped, what it costs, and what it has taken so far.
subsNameHint: Pick Horizon's guess from the price, or type the right name. It then shows everywhere this payment appears, and holds for your next statement.
rechargeIntro: Your prepaid mobile and DTH recharges, by operator: the plan you are on, when it runs out, and what it comes to a month. Wifi and postpaid bills are left out.
rechargeMetaDescription: Your prepaid mobile and DTH recharges: the plan you are on, when it runs out, and what it costs a month.
rechargeTileMonthlyNone: No plan running in what your statements show
rechargeTileNextNone: Nothing due in what your statements show
rechargeLapsed: It ran out around {date}, and your statements show no recharge after it. Paid from another account, or stopped?
rechargeLeftOut_one: Left out: {count} payment with GST on top, so a wifi or postpaid bill, not a recharge ({list}).
rechargeLeftOut_other: Left out: {count} payments with GST on top, so wifi or postpaid bills, not recharges ({list}).
rechargeNone: No recharges found in your statements.
rechargeDaysLabel: How many days does the {amount} {operator} plan last?
rechargeDaysHint: Horizon guesses from the price (₹349 on Jio is a 28-day plan). The days set what a month costs and when the next one is due.
